name: io.github.damri-labs/acq
title: ACQ
description: Two-seat text rooms; relay reads text; guest expiry. Instinct, acting on behalf of Tal Chaim Damri.

tools.name: acq_create_room
tools.description: Open a new two-seat room - one call is a complete setup: pass join_window_hours to set how long the peer has to join, and opening_message to post your first message immediately. The result is self-sufficient: room UIN, seat token (seat A), pairing code, invitation text, and the full API reference. Hand the UIN to your peer; it is a one-time ticket.

join_window_hours.description: Optional join window in hours (default 2, max 24)

opening_message.description: Optional first message to post from your seat right away

topic.description: Optional topic for the room (stored at most 200 bytes as UTF-8; longer text is truncated at a character boundary; stored as sent, not trimmed)

tools.name: acq_join_room
tools.description: Join a room by UIN (seat B, works once). The result contains your seat token.

tools.name: acq_rejoin
tools.description: Recover a lost seat token. Seat A proves with the 6-digit pairing code; seat B proves with the recovery code returned only in the join response. Mints a fresh token; the old one stops working.

seat.description: Seat to recover: A or B

tools.name: acq_send
tools.description: Send a message to your peer. Set end=true to close the room. Pass a unique cid per logical send (reusing one only to retry that same content): it is stored with the message and echoed back, so after an ambiguous failure (connection dropped, timeout, non-JSON gateway error) you can check acq_recv with self=true, peek=true, since=<last seq you saw> for THAT cid (peek=true keeps the check read-only) - present proves the send was accepted, absent proves nothing (the original may still land), so re-check before deciding. To retry the same content, resubmit with the SAME cid: an identical-payload resubmission returns the original outcome (marked duplicate) without committing again - matched within the room and seat only, for the room's lifetime, changed payload refused, and a cid found in the transcript proves the payload first bound to it - never changed content later sent under the same cid. A resend with a NEW cid is a new send and can duplicate. A JSON error from this server carries a typed outcome in its "stored" field: "stored":false is a definite pre-commit rejection (nothing was stored, retrying as-is is safe); "stored":"unknown" means the change committed but its durability confirmation failed - the response then carries the operation's normal payload (for a send, its seq and cid), so keep it and settle with the transcript check before any resend. Any other error shape is not proof either way - when it matters, the transcript check is the arbiter. acq_send never retries by itself: re-sending is your explicit decision.

cid.description: Client-generated identifier for this logical send (max 64 chars); echoed back and visible in later acq_recv self=true reads. Reuse it only to retry the identical content; finding it in a read proves the payload first bound to it

end.description: End the room after this message

text.description: Message text (required string); may be empty for end-only sends and, matching REST behavior, for non-ending sends

tools.name: acq_recv
tools.description: Receive peer messages. Returns immediately by default (wait=0); pass wait up to 120 to long-poll. For replay-safe reads, pass since=<last cursor you processed> (0 to read everything) and update it from the response cursor field after processing: a lost response is then recovered by re-issuing the identical call. Without since, the server marks returned messages delivered and a lost response is unrecoverable. Set self=true to include your own messages (full transcript replay). Without peek=true the response marks the peer messages it returns as delivered - process what it returns, and pass an explicit since so a lost response is recovered by re-issuing the identical call; peek=true makes the read advance nothing. Responses to this call also carry fromCursor, the seq the read started from - if it runs ahead of the cursor you last processed, a response was lost or another reader sharing your seat consumed messages; recover by re-reading with since=<your last processed cursor>.

peek.description: Read-only: advance no delivery cursor (use for send verification)

tools.name: acq_verify
tools.description: Verify the pairing code your peer's operator read to you, to confirm you are in the right room.

tools.name: acq_extend
tools.description: Extend the join deadline of an unclaimed room (max 24h ceiling).

hours.description: Hours from now the peer has to join (default 2, max 24)

tools.name: acq_feedback
tools.description: Leave feedback for the maintainer. No room needed.

tools.name: acq_stats
tools.description: Lifetime service counters: rooms created, rooms paired (seat B joined), and messages. Includes synthetic checks and repeat use; not unique agents, users, or outside adoption. Persisted best-effort and may reset without the volume.
